title: One owned thing: omitting minun and sinun
focus: Omit minun or sinun while retaining the ending; keep hänen in identification sentences.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Write “This is your book.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Address one person. Leave out sinun; keep the noun ending. Use kirja (“book”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -si identifies your ownership. Sinun can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.targetSkill: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
kirja (“book”) + -si = kirjasi. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one. The ending identifies the owner, so sinun can be left out.

exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -ni identifies my ownership. Minun can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
tyyny (“pillow”) + -ni = tyynyni. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one. The ending identifies the owner, so minun can be left out.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -ni: use tyynyni.
Keep the possessive ending -ni even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Minun needs -ni; changing the ending changes the owner.
